title: Tag upgrade-related incidents + auto-link upgrade diagnostics bundles in Slack threads
author: Jacob Stein
release_notes: Incident-bot now detects upgrade-related incidents and posts diagnostics bundle locations (when available) to the Slack incident thread.
description:
Context: During Private upgrade rehearsals and customer upgrades, we’ve had incidents where responders lose time figuring out whether the issue is upgrade-related and where the relevant upgrade diagnostics bundle lives. This PR adds (1) a lightweight heuristic + explicit override to tag incidents as upgrade-related, and (2) an automated Slack thread reply that links (or points) to the diagnostics bundle location and the upgrade correlation id when present.

What this does: - Adds an `upgrade_related` incident tag that can be set explicitly via incident creation payload (`metadata.upgrade_related=true`) OR inferred via heuristics (title contains "upgrade"/"rollback"/"private installer", or incident label includes `private-upgrade`). - Adds support for `metadata.upgrade_correlation_id` and `metadata.diagnostics_bundle_uri` fields. When present, incident-bot posts a thread message with: correlation id, bundle URI (sanitized), and quick instructions for fetching. - If the bundle URI is an internal object-store path, we post the path only (no pre-signed URL) to avoid accidentally widening access in Slack; responders can use `diagctl fetch <uri>` (internal) or follow the runbook. - Adds a fallback search path: if correlation id is present but diagnostics bundle uri is missing, attempt to locate the latest bundle for the correlation id in our diagnostics index (best-effort; non-blocking).

Operator UX in Slack: - Incident-bot thread reply format is consistent and easy to scan: "Upgrade-related: yes/no", "Correlation ID", "Diagnostics", "Next steps". - For upgrade-related incidents, the bot also adds a short reminder to check the upgrade dashboard panel (Grafana link) and to attach the installer precheck report if available.

Implementation notes: - New module `src/enrichment/upgrade.ts` that computes `upgrade_related` and extracts upgrade metadata from the incident payload. - `src/slack/messages.ts` gains `renderUpgradeContextMessage()` and is wired in the incident creation/update flow. - `src/diagnostics/index.ts` adds a best-effort lookup by correlation id; failures are logged and do not fail incident creation. - All Slack posts are idempotent via a deterministic message key (incident_id + "upgrade_context_v1") to avoid spam on retries.

Security/privacy: - We do NOT generate pre-signed URLs from incident-bot. We only post URIs/paths and instructions. - We redact query params and tokens if the incoming URI includes them. - If the incident is marked customer-facing, we do not post any internal bucket names; we post only "Diagnostics bundle collected" and prompt responders to retrieve via internal tooling.

Testing: - Unit tests cover heuristic classification, explicit override precedence, redaction/sanitization, and message formatting. - Integration test in `__tests__/slack-posts.test.ts` verifies idempotency behavior (retries do not duplicate the message).

Rollout plan: - Deploy behind feature flag `INCIDENTBOT_UPGRADE_CONTEXT_ENABLED` (default off). - Enable first in staging for the next upgrade rehearsal; then enable in prod for SRE on-call.

Related: - ENG-2321 (Upgrade telemetry + diagnostics bundle) - SUP-1842 (customer upgrade incident: missing diagnostics link in incident thread)

Checklist: - [x] Adds unit tests - [x] Staging verified - [x] No new secrets - [x] Slack message redaction verified
commits: incident: add upgrade enrichment fields + heuristics
slack: render upgrade context thread message + idempotency key
diagnostics: best-effort lookup by upgrade correlation id
tests: cover redaction + classification + retry behavior
docs: add runbook snippet reference in bot message templates
review_conversation: Owen Phillips: Please make sure we don’t post pre-signed URLs into Slack. We’ve been burned by that before. Prefer posting the internal URI and a retrieval command.
Jacob Stein (author): Agreed. Updated to never generate signed URLs. We only post sanitized URIs and instructions; also added a guard for customer-facing incidents to avoid internal bucket names.
Allison Grant: Can we ensure message spam doesn’t happen on retry? We see Slack API timeouts occasionally and incident-bot retries.
Jacob Stein (author): Added idempotency with a deterministic message key stored in the incident record. Integration test added to verify no duplicates on retry.
Sean Gallagher: Heuristic classification looks a bit broad ("upgrade" could hit irrelevant incidents). Can we require either label match or presence of correlation id unless explicitly overridden?

Jacob Stein (author): Good call. I tightened it: the title heuristic now only applies when the incident service is one of [private-installer, private-control-plane, private-gateway] OR label includes private-upgrade. Otherwise it won’t auto-tag unless explicitly set.
Rafael Mendes: Please include a link to the Private upgrade runbook section for diagnostics collection.
Jacob Stein (author): Added a stable docs link in the Slack message template and updated `docs/ops/incident-bot.md`.
Owen Phillips: Approved after the signed-url change and tightened heuristic.
